title: Genuinely novel task: no precedent anywhere in the repository's history

known_failed_approach.description: This scenario is not a known-bad-approach trap; it tests behaviour when history exists but is genuinely unrelated (docs-only) to a genuinely novel task. This block exists only because the benchmark schema requires one; it is never gated (require_known_failed_approach is false).

expected_evidence.description: After burn-in the treatment history holds one real Shard for a docs-only change (README.md), touching no code file. The first two generic checks (min_shards; a shard whose task mentions 'license' and whose files are README.md only) are expected to pass and confirm the burn-in was genuinely captured. The third generic check, retrievable_via_relevant_context, is a positive-retrievability assertion and is EXPECTED TO READ FALSE here: relevant_context(evaluation prompt) returns ZERO matches by design -- the burn-in task shares no non-stopword vocabulary with the evaluation task at all (unlike Scenario 5, where the project name alone yields a weak nonzero score). Because that sub-check folds into the overall 'present' flag, 'present' will also read false for this scenario; require_expected_evidence is therefore false so the run is not aborted for achieving exactly the zero-match outcome it exists to test. The scenario's own tests assert the zero-match result directly against real captured history.

notes: The evaluation prompt (relay watch) names no files and is unrelated to README.md or licensing.

Confirmed directly with a synthetic history entry before finalizing this scenario: relevant_context(evaluation_prompt) returns 0 matches against the burn-in Shard, and context_text reads 'No relevant prior OpenShard history found for this task.' -- this is the one scenario in this set where that literal claim holds; Scenario 5 documents why it could not achieve the same with a code-adjacent burn-in task.

The watch command is verified black-box (a real subprocess, the queue file mutated, stdout polled with bounded waits and the process always killed in a finally block) rather than assuming any internal API shape, since the evaluation prompt does not mandate one. Confirmed directly: the base commit fails fast (no hang), a correct implementation passes in under 2 seconds.

Expected effect: a harm/null-condition test. Treatment's .openshard/ history is non-empty but relevant_context is empty for this task -- treatment should behave identically to control, receiving no evidence to use either way.

Revision (2026-09-04): a live attempt aborted with burn_in_evidence_missing. Root cause: this scenario had require_expected_evidence: true, but the benchmark's generic expected-evidence check includes a positive retrievability sub-check (the burn-in Shard must appear in relevant_context(evaluation prompt)) that a zero-match scenario cannot satisfy by definition -- the captured Shard was real and matched on task/files; only that sub-check failed. Fixed by setting require_expected_evidence: false (the same choice Scenario 5 already made for the same reason) and stating the expected read-out above. Nothing about the burn-in prompt, evaluation prompt, hidden verification, or the shared harness changed, and the prior history was not made artificially retrievable.
